drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We propose August 14, 2026 as the firm date for completing production and delivering the privilege log, subject to confirmation before service and without altering any earlier court-ordered deadline. The revised language expressly includes responsive ESI within a reasonable search and makes clear that supplementation does not extend the production deadline. We will provide a request-by-request schedule specifying each objection and its grounds, whether responsive materials are being withheld, and the applicable completion date. We have also removed the unsupported reference to an attached privilege log; the log will identify the applicable requests and provide sufficient information to assess each privilege claim without revealing protected content.

edits.text: 1. REQUEST-SPECIFIC RESPONSES AND OBJECTIONS. Defendant will state separately for each request whether production will be made, the specific legal and factual grounds for any objection, whether responsive materials are being withheld on that basis, and the scope of any withholding. Any objection limited to part of a request will identify that part, and Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged materials responsive to the remainder. No general objection substitutes for these request-specific statements.

2. SEARCH AND PRODUCTION. Defendant will conduct a reasonable search for responsive documents and electronically stored information within its possession, custody, or control. The search will encompass sources and custodians reasonably likely to contain responsive information. Defendant will complete production of responsive, non-privileged materials by August 14, 2026, except for materials expressly identified as withheld in its request-specific responses. Each request-specific response will state that completion date and identify any responsive materials withheld on an asserted objection. Nothing in this response modifies an earlier court-ordered deadline.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. By August 14, 2026, Defendant will provide a log of materials withheld or redacted on attorney-client privilege or work-product grounds. For each entry, the log will identify the applicable request number(s), a unique identifier, the date, document type, author, recipients and their relevant roles, a description of the subject matter that does not disclose protected content, the protection asserted, and sufficient facts to assess that claim. The log will distinguish full withholding from redaction. Defendant will produce reasonably segregable, non-protected portions of responsive materials.

4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement or correct its responses as required by applicable rules or court order. This obligation does not extend the production or privilege-log deadline, authorize deferral of the reasonable search, or excuse timely production of materials located through that search.
